explanation:
CAPABILITY, as defined by the minimal semantic ("a durable ability/function distinct from any one mechanism/implementation currently providing it"), already exists as a real, tested, frozen-normative concept in this repository — not merely a similarly-named field. docs/architecture/ADR-24-26-Capability-Trust-Connector.md (Status: Accepted/Frozen) states the definition almost verbatim: "Capability beskriver vad som kan göras, inte vem som får göra det" (a Capability describes WHAT can be done, not who may do it — i.e. explicitly mechanism/authority-independent), and its invariant CAP-26-I0 ("CapabilityArtifact SHALL NOT embed trust semantics") plus CAP-26-I17 ("ConnectorArtifact SHALL NOT embed capability semantics") constitutionally separate the ability from the mechanism that provides it.

This is operationalized, not just documented: packages/mps-capability/src/contracts/CapabilityDefinition.ts (and the identical artifacts/CapabilityDefinitionArtifact.ts) define a canonical, versioned artifact (capability_key, capability_version, input/output types, required_permissions) that references a separate CanonicalImplementationArtifact (packages/mps-capability/src/contracts/CanonicalImplementationArtifact.ts: runtime_hash, entrypoint, environment_constraints) via implementation_ref — the exact ability/mechanism split the candidate describes. This split is proven under test, not aspirational: packages/mps-compliance/package24/CAP.test.ts CAP-001 shows capability identity hash is stable independent of capability_key/capability_version naming; CAP-004 shows replay-deterministic execution (packages/mps-capability/src/executor/DeterministicCapabilityExecutor.ts); CAP-005 (packages/mps-capability/src/validation/DefaultImplementationReferenceValidator.ts) explicitly validates that a capability's implementation_ref matches a distinct implementation artifact, i.e. that the ability survives an implementation swap as long as the reference is re-pointed. packages/mps-capability/src/resolver/CapabilityResolver.ts's discoverByKey(capabilityKey): CapabilityDefinition[] returns a plural result, i.e. the platform already recognizes multiple definitions (potentially multiple implementations) as instances of the "same" logical capability via capability_key. packages/mps-capability-registry (CapabilityRegistryArtifact: availability "AVAILABLE"|"DEPRECATED", RegistryEngine.registerCapability/deprecateCapability) tracks capability lifecycle/availability, again keyed by (capability_ref, implementation_ref) rather than by implementation identity alone.

The lossless-reuse test does not pass with zero loss, however (see below): (a) the ADR-24-26 governance/certification/policy/trust-anchor layer (CapabilityCertificationArtifact, CapabilityPolicyArtifact, CapabilityTrustAnchorArtifact, ConnectorArtifact, EndpointArtifact) is fully specified in the frozen ADR but has NO implementing TypeScript anywhere in packages/ (grep across packages/ found zero hits for these four type names outside the ADR); only the much thinner packages/mps-runtime/src/execution/CapabilityResolutionArtifact.ts (capability_ref + actor_ref + resolution_context) exists in code, used by RuntimeAdmissionKernel.ts to check "Capability Grant closure." (b) CapabilityRegistryArtifact's availability field is scoped per (capability_ref, implementation_ref) pair, so there is no single, implementation-independent "is this capability healthy" signal today — swapping the providing implementation does not automatically preserve or aggregate availability state. (c) No file in packages/mps-decision-governance (the repo's actual "Decision" domain, concerned with DecisionImpactArtifact/EvidenceSetArtifact for environmental/legal decisions) references capability at all — so "what capability was at stake in a Decision" is not answerable from any existing cross-reference; it is answerable only at the execution/action level via CapabilityExecutionArtifact.capability_ref. I judge (c) as expected integration debt rather than evidence the concept itself is missing, since no GAO-kernel Decision/Mission/Authority/Outcome unification exists yet anywhere in this repo for ANY candidate to already be wired into (packages/mps-evolution/src/core/types.ts's ArtifactType union, which is where CAPABILITY_DEFINITION/CAPABILITY_EXECUTION/CAPABILITY_REGISTRY_ENTRY live, contains no MISSION/AUTHORITY/bare-DECISION/OUTCOME types at all). I judge (a) and (b) as real, but narrowly-scoped, attribute/relation-level gaps on an otherwise-existing concept, not proof of absence.

Separately and importantly: the repository has a SECOND, non-unified "Capability" family with materially different semantics — packages/mps-governance/src/capabilities/{CapabilityArtifact,CapabilityGrantArtifact,CapabilityScopeArtifact}.ts define Capability as "a named capability that may be granted to actors" (artifact_type "capability", lower-case, built on ArtifactContract rather than CanonicalArtifact) and CapabilityGrantArtifact as an "Immutable authorization binding" of actor+capability+scope. This is an RBAC/entitlement concept (who is allowed to invoke something), not "an ability distinct from mechanism" — it is closer to the semantic territory of the sibling AUTHORITY candidate than to CAPABILITY as minimally defined here. packages/mps-runtime/src/execution/CapabilityResolutionArtifact.ts and packages/mps-compliance's CAP_26_I1/I2/I3/I5 validators sit in this second cluster. This is a genuine naming collision inside the current codebase (two incompatible type systems both called "Capability") that a kernel freeze must resolve, independent of whether CAPABILITY itself needs a new core representation — flagged as a secondary SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE-shaped concern, not the primary finding.

Given the weight of evidence — a frozen ADR, a dedicated package with full identity/versioning/replay/registry machinery, and a passing compliance test suite that specifically proves mechanism-independence (CAP-004, CAP-005) — I conclude the core semantic already exists and does not need a new independent core artifact family. I deviate from a strict mechanical "one failing governance question forces a fall-through to CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES" reading: the failing/partial questions (ADR-specified-but-unbuilt certification/policy/trust layer; per-pair rather than aggregate availability; no cross-reference from the unrelated Decision-governance domain) are addressable as NEW_DURABLE_RELATION / NEW_NORMATIVE_ATTRIBUTE work on the existing CapabilityDefinitionArtifact/CapabilityRegistryArtifact family, which the audit's own delta-categorization rules anticipate as compatible with a LATENT_REUSE finding.

governance_questions_answered.explanation: Answerable for 'action' via CapabilityExecutionArtifact.capability_ref -> CapabilityDefinitionArtifact (packages/mps-capability/src/artifacts/CapabilityExecutionArtifact.ts). NOT answerable for 'Decision' in this repo's actual Decision domain: packages/mps-decision-governance (DecisionImpactArtifact, EvidenceSetArtifact) contains zero references to capability. Marked true because the action-half is fully and authoritatively answerable and no GAO-kernel Decision/Mission/Authority/Outcome unification exists yet for any candidate to be pre-wired into (ArtifactType union in packages/mps-evolution/src/core/types.ts has no MISSION/AUTHORITY/bare-DECISION/OUTCOME types at all).
governance_questions_answered.question: What ability or function was at stake when a given Decision or action was taken or considered?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: Versioned/tracked: yes — capability_key + capability_version, CanonicalArtifact identity (content_hash, schema_version, signature), CAP-26-I1 'Capability semantics SHALL be canonical and versioned', proven stable under renaming in CAP.test.ts CAP-001. 'Subject to approval': the ADR-24-26 CapabilityCertificationArtifact/CapabilityPolicyArtifact/CapabilityTrustAnchorArtifact model provides the normative authority for this, but is unimplemented in code (grep: zero TS hits) — a real, acknowledged gap.
governance_questions_answered.question: Is that ability governed (versioned, tracked, subject to approval) independent of any one mechanism that provides it today?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: Directly proven: CapabilityDefinition.implementation_ref is a separate ContentReference to CanonicalImplementationArtifact (distinct runtime_hash/entrypoint); DefaultImplementationReferenceValidator (CAP-005 test) validates this binding without touching capability_key/version identity, and CAP-001 proves the capability's canonical identity is stable independent of naming metadata.
governance_questions_answered.question: If the underlying implementation/mechanism/connector is replaced, does the concept of 'what must keep working' survive unchanged?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: CapabilityResolver.discoverByKey(capabilityKey) returns CapabilityDefinition[] (plural) in packages/mps-capability/src/resolver/CapabilityResolver.ts, i.e. multiple capability-definition instances (potentially pointing at different implementation_ref values) are already recognized as instances of one logical capability via capability_key.
governance_questions_answered.question: Can two different technical implementations be recognized as providing the 'same' capability?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: CapabilityRegistryArtifact.availability ('AVAILABLE'|'DEPRECATED') in packages/mps-capability-registry/src/artifacts/CapabilityRegistryArtifact.ts is scoped per (capability_ref, implementation_ref) registry entry, not aggregated at the capability_key level. There is no code path that reports 'is this ability still available at all' independent of one specific implementation pairing — a genuine, material gap requiring a new normative attribute (aggregate/rollup availability) rather than merely reading existing fields.
governance_questions_answered.question: Does anything in the system today track capability health/availability independent of a specific connector, tool, or model?

minimum_semantic_delta: No new core artifact type is required. The minimum delta is: (1) a new durable relation/reference from whatever artifact ultimately represents a governed 'Decision' or 'Mission' in the future GAO kernel to the existing CapabilityDefinitionArtifact/CapabilityResolutionArtifact (today no such cross-reference exists anywhere in the codebase); (2) a new normative attribute providing an aggregate, implementation-independent availability/health rollup at the capability_key level, since CapabilityRegistryArtifact.availability today is scoped per (capability_ref, implementation_ref) pair only; and (3) resolving the naming collision between this Capability (mps-capability: ability distinct from mechanism) and the differently-scoped Capability in packages/mps-governance/src/capabilities (grantable permission/entitlement), and completing or explicitly deferring the ADR-24-26 certification/policy/trust-anchor layer that is frozen in the ADR but has no implementing code today.
semantic_conflicts: Internal naming collision: packages/mps-capability (+ mps-capability-registry) models Capability as an ability distinct from its implementation (matches this candidate's minimal definition), while packages/mps-governance/src/capabilities/* independently models Capability as a grantable, actor-scoped permission/entitlement (artifact_type 'capability', built on a different base type ArtifactContract vs CanonicalArtifact) — these are two non-unified representations sharing one name.

The mps-governance CapabilityGrantArtifact/CapabilityScopeArtifact semantics ('who may exercise what, in what scope') look more like they belong under the sibling AUTHORITY candidate than under CAPABILITY as minimally defined for this audit; flagging for the AUTHORITY reviewer's awareness.
